title: Package exposure drops Cabal reexported-modules: consumers can't import re-exported modules (effectful: import Effectful)
description: REPORTED by crucible adopting effectful. effectful's CLOSURE compiles fine (monad-control/strict-mutable-base pins honoured, all .hi built+registered). The failure is package EXPOSURE to a consumer: 'import Effectful' in a consumer fails 'module not found'. ROOT CAUSE (confirmed against this machine's store + src): the 'Effectful' module is NOT in the 'effectful' package — it is exposed by 'effectful-core' (store dir d8a4c52b, id effectful-core, exposed-modules includes 'Effectful'). The 'effectful' package (store dir 1a790cc, id effectful) re-exports the core API via Cabal 'reexported-modules:' so that 'build-depends: effectful' + 'import Effectful' works. zinc DROPS reexported-modules end-to-end: (1) Zinc.Cabal reads exposedModules (Cabal.hs:236) but never reexportedModules; (2) Build.PackageConf has no confReexportedModules field; (3) renderConf (Build.hs:90-104) never emits a 'reexported-modules:' line; (4) grep reexport src/ = NONE. So zinc's generated effectful .conf lists only effectful's OWN modules (Effectful.Process, Effectful.FileSystem, ...) and omits the reexports (Effectful, Effectful.Dispatch.*, Effectful.State.*, ...). With -hide-all-packages + -package-id effectful, GHC can't see 'Effectful' -> module not found. NOT a store collision: the reporter's smoking gun (one dir holds Effectful.hi + Paths_effectful_core.hi) is dir d8a4c52b = effectful-core ALONE, correctly keyed (BuildKey includes bkName, zinc-qln); Effectful.hi legitimately belongs to effectful-core. Why the agent's 'effectful probe' e2e passed: the probe imported effectful-OWNED modules (not the re-exported 'Effectful'), so it never exercised reexports. FIX: model reexported-modules — read Library.reexportedModules in Zinc.Cabal, add confReexportedModules to PackageConf, render 'reexported-modules:' in renderConf (ghc-pkg format: 'OrigPkg:OrigName as NewName' / bare name for same-name). effectful-core stays registered in the db (it is), so GHC follows the reexport without the consumer needing -package-id effectful-core. CLASS: blocks ANY reexporting/umbrella package (very common: effectful, monorepo facades). SECOND SYMPTOM TO VERIFY: flat project (members=["."]) fails EARLIER with 'cannot satisfy -package-id effectful' — confirm whether same root cause or a separate flat-layout exposure/ordering bug; split if separate. Relates: qln (monorepo subdir/clone-share, closed).
notes: PRIORITIZED (2026-06-06, planner): real-world adoption blocker (crucible) — take this BEFORE the open wasm (9po.5/.6) and deploy (nbk.2/.3/.4) work. ACCEPTANCE TEST (the case the 'effectful probe' e2e missed): a consumer workspace declaring ONLY 'effectful' as a dependency, whose library does 'import Effectful' (the RE-EXPORTED module, owned by effectful-core) and uses an effectful-core symbol, must compile + run. Verify BOTH layouts: two-level workspace AND flat (members=["."]) — the flat path currently fails earlier ('cannot satisfy -package-id effectful'); confirm whether the reexported-modules fix resolves it or it is a separate flat-layout exposure bug, and split if separate. Also add a regression fixture so reexports stay covered. Companion: zinc-rxa (verbose GHC passthrough) lands the visibility to debug this quickly.
close_reason: DONE + verified e2e (2026-06-06). zinc now honours Cabal reexported-modules end-to-end. (1) Zinc.Cabal reads Library.reexportedModules into Component.compReexports as (newName, originPkg?, originName). (2) buildLibArtifactsFor resolves each reexport's origin unit-id — the explicit pkg if named, else the dep registered in the db that exposes the origin module — and sets PackageConf.confReexports. (3) renderConf emits them inline in exposed-modules using ghc-pkg's 'New from unit:Orig' syntax (empirically confirmed: a consumer with only -package-id <umbrella> imports the re-exported module). ACCEPTANCE TEST PASSED (the case the earlier effectful probe missed): a FLAT (members=[.]) consumer depending ONLY on effectful, doing 'import Effectful (runPureEff)' (Effectful is owned by effectful-core, re-exported by effectful) + using an effectful-core symbol, builds + runs (prints 42). Flat-layout 'cannot satisfy -package-id effectful' symptom did NOT reproduce — it was a downstream effect of the missing reexports, resolved by this fix (no separate flat bug). Unit tests: Cabal reexport read + renderConf 'from' rendering; full suite 391/0. NOTE: surfaced + fixed a sib regression (preemptive boot-conflict over-firing blocked effectful via unliftio-core's advisory base bound) — see zinc-sib correction note.

title: GHC diagnostics truncated + ghc-options/-v passthrough swallowed: can't see full compiler error on build failure
description: REPORTED by crucible while debugging effectful exposure. On a build failure zinc truncates GHC's diagnostic, and there is no way to get the full output: '-v' is not a zinc flag, and target ghc-options=["-v"] got swallowed (not forwarded to the member compile). A consumer hitting a -package-id / module-not-found error can't see the exact id mismatch, blocking self-service debugging. WANT: (1) a verbosity/passthrough so the full GHC stderr is shown (e.g. zinc build -v / --verbose, or ZINC_VERBOSE), and (2) ensure ghc-options (incl. -v) declared in zinc.toml [build]/target actually reach the member ghc --make invocation. Pairs with the agent-devex diagnostics core (rdy/unv): the typed diagnostic should be able to attach/redirect to the raw tool output on demand.

title: zinc add: deterministic closure discovery via ghc-pkg + Hackage repo auto-fill
description: Make 'zinc add <pkg>' discover the full transitive closure deterministically instead of the iterative '.cabal-walk -> no repo for X -> add repo -> retry' loop. Design: (1) when <pkg> is in the GHC env, compute its non-boot transitive closure via 'ghc-pkg field <pkg> depends' walked recursively (filter zinc's isBootLib set); (2) for each closure member auto-derive its git repo via the existing Zinc.Hackage.hackageSourceRepo (Hackage source-repository) and pre-populate [registry]; (3) FLAG members whose source-repo is Nothing (e.g. colour, tf-random — darcs-era, no git) as 'needs vendoring'; (4) then resolve+freeze. Caveats: ghc-pkg only knows installed pkgs (fall back to the .cabal-walk resolver otherwise) and reflects the env's cabal-flag choices (use as the authoritative closure for this env / a cross-check). Pieces already exist: Zinc.Hackage.{sourceRepoOf,hackageSourceRepo,hackageCabalUrl}; the recursive ghc-pkg walk is ~15 lines. Motivated by the hspec-closure assembly for zinc-n07.
notes: PARTS 1-3 DONE via the new zinc closure command (Zinc.Closure): ghc-pkg non-boot transitive closure walk + Hackage source-repository auto-fill + needs-vendoring flagging. Pure cores (pkgNameOf, parseDependsField) + injectable discoverRepos are unit-tested; smoke-verified live (optparse-applicative gives the exact 7-pkg closure, colour flagged for vendoring). REMAINING part 4: wire into zinc add so it auto-populates the discovered repos into the manifest, fails if any needs vendoring, then resolve+freeze (changes adds write flow; network-gated). Caveat: ghc-pkg only knows installed pkgs (fall back to the cabal-walk resolver for others).
close_reason: zinc add deterministic closure discovery COMPLETE. Parts 1-3: zinc closure command (ghc-pkg non-boot closure + Hackage repo auto-fill + needs-vendoring flagging). Part 4: wired into zinc add (auto-discovers, refuses if any needs vendoring -> exit 3, else pre-populates repos + freezes). enrichWithRepos respects hand-supplied overrides; sourceRepoOf appends subdir + normalizes git://->https://. Verified live (optparse-applicative/colour vendoring, SHA closure); freeze reuses tested freezeWorkspace (clone network-gated in sandbox). 243 examples, -Wall clean.

title: Discovery fails for monorepo packages whose source-repository omits subdir (effectful)
description:
REPORTED: zinc add effectful fails to resolve. Root cause confirmed against Hackage: effectful, effectful-core, and effectful-th all publish `source-repository head` with `location: https://github.com/haskell-effectful/effectful.git` and NO `subdir:` field -- even though each package lives in its own subdirectory (effectful/, effectful-core/, effectful-th/). So discovery (Zinc.Hackage.sourceRepoOf -> Zinc.Closure) resolves every one of them to the repo ROOT; zinc then tries to build e.g. effectful-core from the root, where there is no effectful-core.cabal, and resolve/build fails.

NOT a parser bug: sourceRepoOf already appends #subdir WHEN the stanza declares `subdir:` (Hackage.hs:46-48, e.g. prettyprinter). The gap is the common monorepo pattern where the published source-repository points at the repo root with no subdir. zinc can't learn the subdir from Hackage metadata alone.

The build-from-subdir machinery already exists: splitRepoSubdir (Zinc.Git) + 576.2 (build a package in a repo subdir) + the manual `repo = ".../effectful.git#effectful-core"` override all work. The gap is purely DISCOVERY inferring the subdir.

Fix direction (to shape): after cloning a discovered repo, if <pkg>.cabal is not at the resolved (sub)path, probe for the conventional <pkg-name>/ subdir (the dominant monorepo layout) and use it; deterministic + shown in the resolution table + frozen in the lock. Fall back to flagging for a manual repo#subdir override (already supported) when the probe can't find it. A curated subdir-overrides table could cover odd layouts later.

Relates: extends 49o (closure discovery, closed); reuses splitRepoSubdir + 576.2 (subdir build, closed). Sibling to b1z (vendoring) as another discovery edge.
notes: PART 1 (discovery subdir) DONE (commit, tree-URL normalization): the real discovery gaps were forge browser tree-URLs (location AND homepage-fallback, e.g. unliftio's homepage https://github.com/fpco/unliftio/tree/master/unliftio#readme) reaching git clone verbatim — now normalized to clone-url#subdir by sourceRepoOf/splitTreeUrl. The <name>/-subdir case the bug described was already handled by packageDirIn's probe at resolve+build. PART 2 (share the monorepo clone across sub-packages by re-keying storeSrcPath by repo-root+rev) STILL PENDING — note contentHash already hashes the full clone tree so per-package shas already match across sub-packages, lowering risk. SEPARATELY: 'zinc add effectful' end-to-end is now blocked by HPACK (unliftio ships package.yaml, no committed .cabal) — filed as zinc-pzu; out of qln scope. qln remains open for PART 2.
close_reason: Both parts done. Part 1 (commit 1): forge tree-URL discovery normalization (location + homepage-fallback + #anchor). Part 2 (commit 2): (a) share ONE clone across a monorepo's sub-packages — storeSrcPath re-keyed by srcKey (repo, not name) with a clone-scoped fetch lock + GC kept consistent; (b) per-package build cache key — BuildKey now includes the package name so siblings sharing a commit don't collide on one pkg-store entry. Verified e2e: 2-pkg monorepo clones once, builds 2 artifacts, runs; self-host 22 pkgs OK. Note: effectful itself still needs hpack (zinc-pzu).

title: C-sources (cbits) objects not archived into the library -> undefined references at link
description: A closure dep with cabal c-sources fails to LINK into a dependent: aeson's closure dies with 'undefined reference to hsprimitive_memset_Word' (primitive) and 'splitmix_init' (splitmix). Root cause: buildLibArtifacts passes c-sources to 'ghc --make' as ABSOLUTE paths (lbMemberDir </> csource); GHC then writes the C object next to the source (src/<pkg>/cbits/foo.o) instead of under -outputdir (verified: a RELATIVE c-source path lands in <outputdir>/cbits/foo.o, an ABSOLUTE one lands next to the source). So findObjs(distDir) never collects it and 'ar' omits it from libHS<pkg>.a -> the C symbols are undefined when a dependent links. Self-host doesn't hit it because nothing references primitive's memset_* / splitmix_init; aeson's closure (via vector/primitive Prim instances) does. It also pollutes the content-addressed src (related to zinc-c3g). Fix: compile c-sources in a separate step into the dist dir (ghc -c <abs.c> -o <distDir>/<rel>.o with the package's include-dirs), and drop them from the --make line, so findObjs archives them and the src stays pristine. Blocks the aeson ffm fixture (zinc-ffm.1).
close_reason: C-sources compiled into dist dir + archived (separate ghc -c step); aeson links. Hermetic regression test.

title: Preprocessor output pollutes content-addressed src -> ContentHashMismatch on rebuild
description: A closure package that ships a preprocessor source (.hsc/.x/.y) has its generated .hs written INTO its source dir by runPreprocessorsIn (Build.hs), mutating the content-addressed src tree under <store>/src/<name>-<rev>. On a later rebuild where the package is NOT in the build cache (e.g. after a failed build, or 'zinc clean' which clears pkg/ but keeps src/), buildNode's verifyFetched recomputes contentHash over the polluted tree and it no longer matches the lock's freeze sha256 -> ContentHashMismatch, masking the real state. Observed while building aeson's closure: after hashable failed compiling, a --json rebuild reported 'expected sha256:a3ab8aaf..., got 96e36792...' for hashable instead of the real compile error. Fix: run preprocessors into a separate generated-source dir (like zinc-gen / -outputdir) and add that to GHC's search path, leaving the fetched src tree pristine; or exclude generated outputs from contentHash. Latent correctness bug for any preprocessor-using dep across clean/rebuild cycles (tests don't catch it because they build from a fresh store each time).
close_reason: Preprocessor output now written to <distDir>/zinc-pp (on -i path), not the content-addressed src; src stays pristine across rebuilds. alex e2e pollution assertion + self-host verified.

title: Closure over-inclusion: pick the .cabal whose name matches the dep (aeson)
description: aeson resolution (past strict) pulls packages that are NOT aeson library deps: vector, unordered-containers, and colour (the no-git-repo blocker, via ansi-terminal). This predates ffm.6 (the old code also used the repo root for a no-#subdir dep). FIX: select the .cabal whose package name: matches the dependency name (not just the first one); and/or have packageDirIn verify the chosen dir holds <dep>.cabal. Symptom packages to check: text-iso8601, these/semialign (haskellari/these monorepo), uuid-types, vector-stream, tasty. Until fixed, aeson cannot resolve a correct closure. Note: even with correct reads, colour may still be a genuine transitive dep of some aeson dep -> then it is the b1z vendoring blocker; verify after this fix.

(1) Name-matched cabal selection: cabalManifest prefers <name>.cabal (namedCabal, case-insensitive) and packageDirIn prefers the dir holding THIS packages <name>.cabal, so a monorepo root with only a siblings cabal no longer shadows the real package. (2) Library-only finalize: parseCabalComponentsForGhc requests ComponentRequestedSpec False False (was True True) when reading a dependency, so finalizePD no longer flips shared flags to keep test-suites buildable and drag test-only deps (QuickCheck/tasty) into library build-depends. +tests; all 3 green fixtures unaffected. REMAINING for aeson: it STILL reaches colour (no upstream git repo) deep in its closure. zincs own reader shows only QuickCheck leaking at top level; the colour/ansi-terminal path runs through subdir-package reads that bash tooling cannot cleanly trace. This is EITHER a genuine transitive dep (-> the b1z vendoring epic: colour has no git repo) OR residual subdir over-inclusion. Definitively pinning it needs a closure PARENT-CHAIN trace (zinc closure --explain-style) which does not exist yet. Cause: vector is pinned to vector-0.13.2.0 but its transitive deps are auto-discovered as Latest (primitive 0.9.1.0, vector-stream 0.1.0.1), and those newer versions are not API-compatible with vector-0.13.2.0 (which shipped against vector-stream 0.1.0.0). zinc has no version solver (one ref per name, Latest = newest tag) so it cannot honour the root .cabal build-depends bounds. Options: (a) FIXTURE-level pin the transitive deps to versions compatible with vector-0.13.2.0 (workaround, gets the fixture green); (b) constrain a discovered Latest by the declaring package .cabal version bounds (a minimal bound check, not a full solver); (c) accept vector as a known-limited fixture. This is the last blocker for the vector ffm fixture build; subdir discovery + macros are done.

So option (a) pinning will not help. The "Couldnt match kind k with *" at Data.Vector G.length is a genuine compile failure that needs real debugging: likely either (i) primitive 0.9.x has a breaking change that vectors <0.10 bound is too optimistic about at GHC 9.6.5, or (ii) a zinc build-pipeline issue (e.g. vector-stream not registered/linked the way vector expects, stale .hi, or a missing ghc-option). Next: capture the FULL error + which package/module, confirm vector-stream built+registered correctly, and try the same trio under cabal to isolate upstream-vs-zinc. Retitle if it turns out to be a zinc build bug rather than upstream incompat.
close_reason: Two root causes fixed: sub-library over-merge (library-only deps) + dropped default-language (poly-kinded phantom). vector fixture builds+runs (55), wired into harness; self-host intact.

title: cabal_macros: emit dep VERSION_ from built closure, not global ghc-pkg
description: Building vector fails: cabal_macros.h defines VERSION_primitive 0.8.0.0 (from emitCabalMacros via installedVersions, which queries the GLOBAL ghc-pkg) while GHC resolves -package primitive to the workspace-built 0.9.1.0, so the CPP redefinition conflicts. emitCabalMacros must source each closure deps version from what zinc actually built/registered (the workspace pkgdb / resolved closure), not the global GHC env. installedVersions queries ghc-pkg list with no --package-db, so it misses the wsDb-registered closure versions. Likely affects any closure whose dep versions differ from the nix-provided GHC global db. Surfaced by the vector ffm fixture (vector-0.13.2.0 + primitive-0.9.1.0). NOTE: may also interact with version-compat (vector 0.13.2.0 vs primitive 0.9.1.0) — verify the version is right, not just the macro.
notes: REFINED DIAGNOSIS (2026-06-05): emitCabalMacros already #ifndef-guards each VERSION_/MIN_VERSION_, and GHC 8.0+ AUTO-GENERATES VERSION_<pkg>/MIN_VERSION_<pkg> for every -package dep (seen as ghc_2.h on <command-line>). zinc includes cabal_macros.h via -optP-include BEFORE GHCs auto macros, so zincs stale 0.8.0.0 (from installedVersions = global ghc-pkg, which lacks the wsDb-built primitive 0.9.1.0) wins the ifndef, then GHCs correct 0.9.1.0 is flagged as a conflicting redefinition. FIX OPTIONS (likely-best first): (1) stop emitting DEP VERSION_/MIN_VERSION_ entirely and rely on GHCs auto macros (keep only the self-package version that Cabal-style code may reference) -- verify a closure still builds; (2) source dep versions from the workspace pkgdb (the built closure) instead of global ghc-pkg so zincs value matches GHCs (no conflicting redefinition). Either removes the redefinition. Validate against the vector fixture (then commit its lock + add it to the ffm integration test). title: Output event model + ReaderT sink + unified OutputMode
description: Foundation (spec s2,s8). (1) OutputEvent sum: ResolveStart, FetchStart/Done{pkg}, CompileStart/Done{pkg,timeMs,cached}, RegisterDone, Finished{summary}; Diagnostic flows through too. (2) Emit via a ReaderT sink over ExceptT ZincError IO -- build code calls emit (CompileDone ...); env carries the sink (cross-cutting plumbing through Orchestrate/Build/Fetch). (3) Resolve ONE OutputMode at the CLI/Main boundary (TTY->human+color, pipe->human plain, --json->machine, --quiet, NO_COLOR) and DROP the per-command --json Bool (CLI.hs + Main.hs refactor). design:
LOCKED 2026-06-05.
SINK: newtype Sink wraps (OutputEvent -> STM ()). Monoid: Sink f <> Sink g emits to both (f e then g e); mempty is the no-op sink (quiet/null). Fan-out composes the output-renderer sink with the metrics-recorder sink; --quiet just drops a term.
CONCURRENCY: a SINGLE renderer thread owns the terminal, the done/total counter and the live progress line. Concurrent producers (produceOne across ~16 threads) ONLY enqueue via writeTQueue. withRenderer forks the render loop, runs the body with the sink, and on ANY exit (success, ZincError, async exception) sets a closed TVar via finally. The render loop drains in STM: readTQueue orElse (closed AND empty implies stop, else retry) so a dying producer cannot deadlock the renderer (no sentinel-never-written bug). takeMVar waits for the drain before returning.
DEP: stm is a GHC boot lib (already in isBootLib) so this adds NO non-boot dependency; just list stm in depends.
MONAD: emit over ReaderT Sink (ExceptT ZincError IO): emit e = ask then liftIO (atomically (runSink s e)). withRenderer/withRecorder installed once at Main, so the sink reaches every runResult boundary from there.
EVENTS: OutputEvent sum: ResolveStart, FetchStart pkg, FetchDone pkg, CompileStart pkg, CompileDone pkg timeMs cached, RegisterDone pkg, Finished summary; a Diagnostic also flows through as an event.
MODE: resolve ONE OutputMode at Main from parsed OutputFlags plus runtime (isatty stdout, NO_COLOR env): TTY gives human+color, pipe gives human plain, --json gives machine, plus --quiet and NO_COLOR.
FLAG ABSTRACTION: bake outputFlags (Parser OutputFlags) into the sub combinator so every subcommand inherits --json/--quiet in the zinc build --json position, declared ONCE. Command constructors DROP their per-command Bool; parseArgs returns (OutputFlags, Command). NO_COLOR is an env var read in resolveMode, not a parser flag.
RECORD UNIFICATION: CompileDone timeMs is the single source for BOTH rendering and metrics; the recorder sink accumulates events and writes metrics.jsonl at end-of-stream, replacing the current end-of-build recordBuild call. Optional in the first pass (recorder may stay end-of-build) but design OutputEvent so a metrics consumer can drain it.
notes: INCREMENT 3 DECISION (2026-06-05, overrides the LOCKED ReaderT monad choice): use an EXPLICIT Sink param threaded through the build path only (runBuildReport/runWarm -> buildClosure -> produceOne), NOT ReaderT over Result. Rationale: events originate ONLY in the resolve/fetch/build subtree; status/doctor/graph/explain/fmt/closure never emit, so an ambient reader over the whole Result monad is plumbing those commands do not use. Keeps the Result type alias and every runResult boundary untouched. User-approved.

title: Real .cabal version for fetched deps (fix hardcoded version=0)
description: loadDepComponents returns version "0" for .cabal-only deps, so a built dep registers as version 0. Under -package-id, GHC auto-generates MIN_VERSION_<dep>/VERSION_<dep> macros from the registered version (0), which then clash with zinc's synthesized cabal_macros.h (real version), e.g. 'VERSION_colour redefined' ("0" vs "2.3.6"). Fix: extract the real package version from the .cabal (Cabal PackageDescription pkgVersion) in Zinc.Cabal and thread it through loadDepComponents so the registered version + macros match (identical redefinition is then harmless). Also makes MIN_VERSION_* correct for CPP guards in real deps.
close_reason: Zinc.Cabal.cabalVersion extracts real version; loadDepComponents uses it; VERSION_colour redefinition gone (confirmed by re-probe). 164 examples, -Wall clean. ansi-terminal-types now advances to the Safe Haskell blocker (576.9) only.

The module itself isn't safe.' colour's modules are normally Safe-inferred, but zinc's compile of colour does not yield a Safe-certified interface (possibly missing default-extensions/flags from the .cabal, or -package-id interaction). Investigate how ghc --make Safe-infers colour under zinc vs cabal; ensure built deps preserve Safe/Trustworthy so safe-importing dependents (ansi-terminal-types) compile. Blocks the optparse-applicative closure for self-host.
notes: DECISION (2026-06-04, see design s1.1 + s3 'build facts/quirks'): do NOT replicate cabal's implicit Safe auto-detection (violates principle 4: reject inference). Be explicit, but the explicit flag is ZINC-AUTHORED data attached to the package (a small version-controlled quirks table shipped with zinc, e.g. colour -> -XTrustworthy), applied automatically + frozen — NOT hand-written by the end user (colour is a 3rd-level transitive dep; principles 2-3). Workspace [build-options] stays as the user-facing override/escape hatch only. DoD for default path: colour builds Safe-importable via zinc's quirks data with the user touching nothing. Forbidden: globally disabling Safe Haskell or blanket -XTrustworthy (principle 4).

title: zinc --version / version: semver + git commit + build date
description:
Expose a proper version in the CLI: a `--version` flag AND a `version` command (cargo/ngrok convention), printing `zinc <semver> (<short-commit>, <date>)`, e.g. `zinc 0.1.0.0 (a1b2c3d, 2026-06-05)`. Falls back to plain `zinc <semver>` (no parenthetical) when commit/date are unavailable. Today neither flag nor command exists; `zinc --version` errors.

SEMVER source of truth = Zinc.Diagnostic.zincVersion ("0.1.0.0"), currently HAND-DUPLICATED in zinc.toml [package] version + flake.nix version -> add a release check that asserts those + the git tag all match zincVersion (stop the 3-way drift).

COMMIT + DATE injected at BUILD time via a small Zinc.BuildInfo module:
  - Nix/flake build: the flake fileset omits .git, so DO NOT git-in-sandbox -- instead pass self.shortRev (or dirtyShortRev) + self.lastModifiedDate from the flake into the derivation (env/arg), and the buildPhase writes them into Zinc.BuildInfo before `ghc -o zinc`.
  - Dev build (ghc directly): capture via `git rev-parse --short HEAD` + date.
  - Fallback: commit/date = Nothing -> plain semver.

Touches CLI.hs (flag + command) + flake.nix (pass self.shortRev/lastModifiedDate) + a new Zinc.BuildInfo module + the JSON envelope (surface commit/date there too). Coordinate with the hw6 CLI rework (CLI.hs is its active file).
notes: STALE: 'tag <-> cabal version' — zinc.cabal was removed. The version now lives in Zinc.Diagnostic.zincVersion ("0.1.0.0", surfaced in every --json envelope's "zinc" field) and zinc.toml [package] version. Re-scope: reconcile a git release tag with zincVersion (single source of truth), e.g. a check or a release script that asserts tag == zincVersion.
close_reason: --version flag + version command + version --json; plain fallback, optional commit/date via CPP; smoke-tested both paths.

title: Boot-library conflict diagnostic: detect stale tag vs toolchain, suggest the compatible commit
description: CLASS (generalised from 57y): upstream's newest release tag is incompatible with a GHC boot library even though a compatible UNTAGGED commit exists -- recurring under zinc's 'no solver, latest tag' model whenever a maintainer is slow to release. Makes real the design's existing promise (cabal-replacement spec line 81: version bounds are 'ignored (at most a warning)'). DEPTH (decided): detect + suggest the EXACT commit. BEHAVIOUR: zinc already reads each dep's .cabal (Opt-2) and already clones the repo. When a closure member's declared bound on a GHC boot library is violated by the toolchain version, emit a typed ZINC_DEP_BOOT_CONFLICT instead of a cryptic 'ErrorT not in scope' GHC failure -- naming the package, its newest tag, the boot lib + both versions. Then probe the default-branch HEAD's .cabal; if it relaxes the bound, the nextAction names that specific commit (e.g. 'pin monad-control to 3785240 -- its HEAD supports transformers 0.6'). PRINCIPLE GUARD: bounds remain ADVISORY metadata only -- read for diagnostics, never fed to resolution. HEAD-probe is NOT a solver (no version-space search): 'your tag is stale; the clone you already have contains a newer compatible commit.' Consistent with line 81 and 'reject inference, not metadata'. HOME: agent-devex diagnostics (extends rdy/unv, both closed).
notes: CORRECTION (2026-06-06, found by zinc-jdf's acceptance test): the original wiring fired the boot-conflict check PREEMPTIVELY (before compiling), which made an ADVISORY cabal bound a hard build-blocker — contradicting this issue's own 'bounds remain advisory' guard. It over-fired on conservative-but-harmless bounds (e.g. unliftio-core's 'base <4.17' vs toolchain base 4.18.2.1), BLOCKING effectful (which compiles fine against base 4.18). FIXED: the check now runs ONLY when a compile actually FAILS — then, if a stale boot-lib bound explains the failure, the cryptic GHC error is replaced with ZINC_DEP_BOOT_CONFLICT (+ HEAD-probe forward-pin). So real breaks (monad-control transformers<0.6 -> ErrorT not in scope) still get the typed diagnostic, but builds that succeed despite a stale upper bound proceed. Also removes the per-package .cabal+ghc-pkg overhead on every clean build (now failure-path only).
close_reason: DONE + verified e2e (2026-06-06). Implemented to decided depth (detect + suggest EXACT commit). (1) Pure detector Zinc.Cabal.bootConflicts: parse+finalize a dep's .cabal, compare each boot-lib build-depends range against the toolchain's installedVersions via Cabal's withinRange; bounds read for DIAGNOSTICS ONLY, never fed to resolution (spec line 81 honoured). (2) New typed ZINC_DEP_BOOT_CONFLICT (exit 3) naming pkg, boot lib + both versions. (3) Wired into Orchestrate.buildNode: fires BEFORE compiling a cabal dep, replacing the cryptic 'ErrorT not in scope' GHC failure. (4) HEAD-probe: on conflict, clones the dep's default HEAD and, if HEAD relaxes the bound, names that exact commit as a copy-paste forward-pin. VERIFIED: 'zinc build' on a workspace at monad-control's stale tag now emits ZINC_DEP_BOOT_CONFLICT and suggests rev=378524047... (the exact 1.0.4 commit 57y needed). Unit tests (bootConflicts 3 + diagnostic 2) + full suite green (381, 0 failures).

title: package static: musl static binary via pkgsStatic
description: zinc package static -> a self-contained static (musl) binary. Honest limit: packages with C FFI/system-libs may not link static -> surface ZINC_STATIC_UNSUPPORTED clearly, not a cryptic linker error. The fiddliest format.
notes:
STATIC CONSTRAINT DETAILS:
1. musl, not glibc. Portable static needs musl libc (glibc static breaks NSS/getaddrinfo via dlopen). => a SEPARATE musl GHC toolchain (nixpkgs pkgsStatic / static-haskell-nix), provisioned via the flake -- structurally the same 'different toolchain' pattern as the wasm target (9po). So 'package static' = a musl build + static link, not just a link flag.
2. HARD BLOCKER (ZINC_STATIC_UNSUPPORTED): closure members with C FFI / extra-libraries / system-libs need a static .a of that C lib; pkgsStatic has many but NOT all, and anything using dlopen/plugins can't be static at all. Pure-Haskell closures link fine; the C-FFI tail is the casualty (mirror of the wasm pure-Haskell-only limit). Flag clearly, don't emit a cryptic linker error.
3. Caveats when it links: musl DNS/NSS (no nsswitch plugins), minimal locales/iconv, libgmp.a gotcha (or use ghc-bignum native backend to drop GMP), larger binaries, heavy toolchain build (want a binary cache).
SHARES the wasm 'provision a different toolchain' machinery (9po.1); the package verb drives a musl build for this format.
close_reason: package static: zinc builds dynamic GHC binaries and can't musl-static-relink them, so surfaces a clear ZINC_STATIC_UNSUPPORTED diagnostic (exit 4) pointing at docker/bundle, not a cryptic linker error. Honest v1 per design.

INVARIANT preserved: one GHC per build -- NO mixing versions within a closure / no per-member ghc (GHC .hi/.o + package-db are ABI-incompatible across versions; members must share one compiler). Pairs with the wasm Target build-dimension pattern (zinc-9po.1): the build is parameterized by (ghc-version, target) and the store keys on both -- generalize Target to carry the GHC version too.

title: Level-parallel closure build scheduler
